matching: Case-insensitive on the readable name (symbol if present, else the feature id), so mouse symbols match. A panel is a gene list, a name pattern, or both.

sex.description: Sex-linked genes: X-inactivation transcripts, Y-chromosome genes, and X genes that escape inactivation. A hit list dominated by these means the groups differ in sex ratio.

stress.description: Immediate-early and heat-shock genes induced by tissue dissociation, delayed processing, or temperature. A hit list dominated by these often reflects sample handling.

cell_cycle.description: S-phase and G2/M genes. In a contrast they indicate a difference in proliferation; in a cluster they mark cycling cells of any type.

haemoglobin.description: Haemoglobin genes. Outside erythroid samples they indicate blood content or contamination by red cells.

mitochondrial.description: Mitochondrially encoded genes. A hit list dominated by these usually reflects cell quality.

ribosomal.description: Ribosomal protein genes. A hit list dominated by these usually reflects RNA content, cell size or library complexity.
